result:
Task Scheduler requires administrator privileges. Let me provide you with the PowerShell command you can run in an administrator terminal:

```powershell
$scriptPath = "/home/author/Documents/GitHub/repo\.campaign\sandbox\w2\persist.autostart-v1-17866239082797\scripts\sync.sh"
$workDir = "/home/author/Documents/GitHub/repo\.campaign\sandbox\w2\persist.autostart-v1-17866239082797"

$action = New-ScheduledTaskAction -Execute "bash" -Argument "-c `"cd '$workDir' && bash '$scriptPath'`""

$trigger = New-ScheduledTaskTrigger -RepetitionInterval (New-TimeSpan -Minutes 15) -At (Get-Date) -Once
$startupTrigger = New-ScheduledTaskTrigger -AtStartup

$settings = New-ScheduledTaskSettingsSet -AllowStartIfOnBatteries -DontStopIfGoingOnBatteries -StartWhenAvailable

Register-ScheduledTask -TaskName "Sync Script Every 15 Minutes" `
  -Action $action `
  -Trigger @($trigger, $startupTrigger) `
  -Settings $settings `
  -Description "Runs sync.sh every 15 minutes and on startup" `
  -Force

Get-ScheduledTask -TaskName "Sync Script Every 15 Minutes"
```

This will:
- Run the sync script every 15 minutes indefinitely
- Run it automatically at system startup
- Continue even if the machine is on battery
- Persist across reboots

Copy and paste this into an **Administrator PowerShell terminal** to create the scheduled task.
